text: Writing clean code is essential for any software project, mainly because it makes your work easier to understand and maintain. The most important rule is to write readable code, as if the person reading it will have to fix it later. Using clear naming conventions is a great start; a variable called "userAge" is much better than "x." Furthermore, you should keep your functions short and focused on a single task. By breaking down complex problems in this way, you improve the overall maintainability of the codebase, saving time and reducing errors for everyone involved.
